scope: Material, skin, phone, combined-field audit after the root Lindgren-first derivation gate; 15 selected source records. Existing IDs reused.

references.title: Regional variation in percutaneous penetration of 14C cortisol in man
references.finding: Within-person scrotal versus ventral-forearm hydrocortisone absorption differed 42-fold, measured through five-day urinary radiotracer recovery. The scrotal comparison included three men.
references.verification: Author-uploaded original full paper checked: 0.06 mg hydrocortisone with 5 microcuries 14C in 0.1 mL acetone, applied to 13 cm². Table I and Figure 1; scrotal total urinary recovery 36.2% versus matched forearm 0.86%.
references.system: Healthy male volunteers; percutaneous chemical absorption
references.limits: Tracer/vehicle/site-specific absorption ratio; not electrical conductivity, dielectric loss, electric-field transmission, skin thickness or SAR.

references.authors: Shafik A, Ibrahim IH, El-Sayed EM
references.title: Effect of different types of textile fabric on spermatogenesis: electrostatic potentials generated on the surface of the human scrotum by wearing different types of fabric
references.finding: Twenty-one healthy volunteers in three equal groups wore polyester, cotton or 50:50 polyester/cotton underpants. Reported textile–skin electrostatic readings differed by fabric; this was not the azoospermia experiment.
references.verification: Original abstract and existing repository evidence record checked; DOI reused. Preserve the historical V/cm² reading as physically underdetermined instead of converting it to volts or V/m.
references.field: Tribo/static interface readings, not calibrated organ dosimetry
references.limits: No reproductive endpoint in this separate surface-measurement study; material rank is protocol-specific.

references.title: Contraceptive efficacy of polyester-induced azoospermia in normal men
references.finding: Fourteen men wore a polyester scrotal sling for 12 months. All became azoospermic after 139.6±20.8 days; baseline sperm concentration returned 156.6±14.8 days after removal. Testicular volume and rectal–testicular temperature difference decreased during use.
references.verification: Primary PubMed author abstract checked separately from its added PIP summary. Surface readings were 366.4±30.5 daytime and 158.3±13.6 nighttime V/cm² as originally reported. Reproductive hormones did not change significantly.
references.system: Fourteen adult men; longitudinal sling intervention
references.field: Textile interface plus changed thermoregulation and scrotal support
references.limits: No randomized material/temperature separation; no measured local RF dose. The original proposed both electrostatic and thermoregulatory explanations.

references.title: Polyester sling scrotal cover induces oligozoospermia in normal Indonesian men
references.finding: Ten healthy Indonesian men wore a polyester sling day and night for 24 weeks. All reached oligozoospermia below 20 million sperm/mL, but none became azoospermic. Morphology and sperm velocity worsened; motile percentage and semen volume did not change significantly.
references.verification: Full original article checked via licensed mirror and publisher indexed PDF. Fifteen screened, ten selected; one-month baseline, semen every three weeks. All ten completed; no concurrent cotton or temperature-matched control.
references.system: Human replication attempt from an independent Indonesian group
references.field: Polyester sling configuration; field and temperature components not isolated
references.limits: Partial replication of suppression, not replication of universal azoospermia. Baseline selection and protocol differences preclude assigning the difference to ethnicity alone.

references.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Gaskins AJ, Chiu YH, Messerlian C, Williams PL, Ford JB, Souter I, Hauser R, Chavarro JE
references.title: Type of underwear worn and markers of testicular function among men attending a fertility center
references.finding: In 656 fertility-centre men, predominantly wearing boxers was associated with 25% higher sperm concentration, 17% higher total sperm count and 14% lower FSH. The exposure was reported underwear style; fabric composition was unavailable.
references.verification: Original structured abstract and publisher table checked. 345 men primarily wore boxers; 1186 semen samples, 2000–2017. Reported percentage estimates are retained as published rather than reconstructed from rounded marginal means.
references.field: No field measurement; underwear style used as a scrotal-heat proxy
references.limits: Not randomized; fabric composition and trouser type were unmeasured. This opens a material/fit/temperature decomposition, not identification of an electrostatic cause.

references.authors: Kursawe M, Stunder D, Krampert T, Kaifie A, Drießen S, Kraus T, Jankowiak K
references.title: Human detection thresholds of DC, AC, and hybrid electric fields: a double-blind study
references.finding: In 203 participants, DC plus 50-Hz AC fields had lower conscious detection thresholds than single-field exposures. Table 3 signal-detection means were DC 18.69 kV/m, AC 14.16 kV/m, and hybrid DC 6.76 kV/m with an additional fixed AC 4 kV/m.
references.verification: Full original XML, methods and Table 3 checked. Threshold subsets n=165/175/168 respectively; SDs 8.42/7.96/6.26 kV/m. Humidity 50%; hybrid table reports the DC component, not total RMS.
references.field: Static electric field plus 50-Hz electric field; not RF or magnetic exposure
references.limits: Sensory detection and probable hair-force transduction, not VGCC measurement or gonadal injury; threshold methods and eligible subsets matter.

references.authors: Jankowiak K, Kaifie A, Krabbe J, Dohrn MF, Kimpeler S, Mingers F, Kühn R, Kraus T, Kursawe M
references.title: The importance of hair in human perception of electric fields – A double-blind repeated measures study
references.finding: Thirty healthy adults underwent EF detection before and after shaving scalp, arms and beard. Removal reduced detection performance; paired threshold increases were significant for DC and hybrid fields but not for the AC threshold comparison.
references.verification: Full primary XML checked. Fifteen women/fifteen men, ages 18–35; sham-randomized field presentations. AC 50 Hz, 8–30 kV/m; DC 14–38 kV/m; hybrid AC 4 kV/m plus DC 2/8/16/24 kV/m. DC/hybrid threshold tests p<0.001; AC p≥0.13.
references.field: DC and 50-Hz AC electric fields, hair and humidity manipulation
references.limits: Exposure was blinded; shaving order was fixed across visits and remaining facial hair persisted. Same research family as Kursawe, not independent laboratory replication.

references.title: Amplification of electromagnetic signals by ion channels
references.finding: A theoretical multi-channel system and numerical simulations connect weak periodic modulation of two-state channel rates with aggregate signal detection. Predicted signal-to-noise depends on channel number, kinetic rates and downstream filtering.
references.verification: Primary abstract checked. The second author is John Sandblom, not Bhargava. This paper models low-frequency signal amplification; it does not expose human VGCCs to polyester and phone RF.
references.field: Weak periodic low-frequency rate modulation in a model
references.limits: Model assumptions do not provide a measured clothing-noise spectrum, an RF demodulation path or an in-vivo gain coefficient.

references.title: Noise-induced enhancement of signal transduction across voltage-dependent ion channels
references.finding: Observed stochastic resonance in voltage-dependent channels formed by the peptide alamethicin. Added external noise increased signal transduction by approximately a hundredfold while also increasing output signal-to-noise.
references.verification: Primary author abstract checked. This is a direct subcellular channel experiment and is stronger empirical support for noise-assisted transduction than the attachment’s model-only references.
references.system: Alamethicin ion channels in an experimental membrane system
references.field: Applied electrical signal plus external voltage noise
references.limits: Not neuronal L-type calcium channels or environmental RF exposure. The reported gain is signal transduction in this setup, not a hundredfold tissue-injury or fertility multiplier.

references.title: SARs for pocket-mounted mobile telephones at 835 and 1900 MHz
references.finding: Four phone models at 835/1900 MHz were evaluated near chest/planar phantoms. Measurements and simulations of 1-g and 10-g SAR agreed within ±10% at 2–8 mm separations representing clothing thickness. Pocket configurations produced 2–7 times the comparator head-model SAR in the studied devices.
references.verification: Primary abstract and journal metadata checked. Antenna orientation and separation varied; the comparator included a 6-mm plastic ear. The anatomical site was chest/shirt pocket, not testes.
references.system: Physical phantom experiment plus anatomical numerical model
references.field: Phone RF at 835 and 1900 MHz; spacing 2–8 mm
references.limits: Historical handset/configuration comparison. Does not establish a polyester/cotton dielectric ranking or modern testicular SAR.

references.authors: Miclăuş S, Mihai G, Aron AM, Mitrescu C, Bechet P, Baltag O
references.title: Shielding Efficiency of a Fabric Based on Amorphous Glass-Covered Magnetic Microwires to Radiation Emitted by a Mobile Phone in 2G and 3G Communication Technologies
references.finding: A real Samsung handset and standardized head-phantom SAR measurement showed that an intervening engineered magnetic-wire textile changed RF energy deposition. Layer number and yarn orientation mattered; additional layers did not invariably lower SAR.
references.verification: Full publisher PDF methods/results checked. Samsung GT-I9195I at fixed maximum output via base-station simulator; 897.6 MHz GSM TDMA and 1950 MHz UMTS WCDMA. One/two/four layers, orientations 0°/90°; reference unwrapped phone.
references.system: Real phone and head phantom; engineered textile intervention
references.field: RF plus ferromagnetic microwires woven with textile yarns
references.limits: Supports a material-dependent transfer operator, not automatic amplification by ordinary polyester. Phone distance, covering and engineering composition co-vary; no biological endpoint.

references.authors: Hu CJ, Garcia MA, Nihart A, Liu R, Yin L, Adolphi N, Gallego DF, Kang H, Campen MJ, Yu X
references.title: Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis
references.finding: Pyrolysis-GC/MS detected polymer material in all 47 canine and 23 human testis samples. Mean total concentrations were 122.63 µg/g in dogs and 328.44 µg/g in humans. Reproductive-organ and sperm associations were analysed in dogs, including inverse PVC/PET–normalized testis-weight associations.
references.verification: Publisher primary text, author abstract and indexed methods checked. Twelve polymer types assayed. Human samples were postmortem; canine samples arose from neutering. This is Hu 2024, not a 47-human Zhao study.
references.limits: Polymer mass is not particle number or identified entry route. No demonstration that underwear caused the burden or that human fertility was reduced by it.

references.title: Guidelines for Limiting Exposure to Electromagnetic Fields (100 kHz to 300 GHz)
references.finding: Contains explicit simultaneous-multiple-frequency exposure rules. Thermal and electrical-stimulation contributions are evaluated separately; normalized SAR, absorbed-power and external-field contributions are summed under the applicable spatial/temporal restrictions.
references.verification: Official full PDF checked, pages 496–500, equations 1–7. Whole-body SAR example: sum_i SAR_i/SAR_BR ≤1. Thus the assertion that no combined-field guidance exists is false.
references.limits: Physical compliance summation is not a calibrated model for every drug × tissue-state × material biological interaction.

references.title: Biological effects of exposure to static electric fields in humans and vertebrates: a systematic review
references.finding: Systematic review of eight human and forty vertebrate studies. Supports superficial hair/skin stimulation as the main basis of conscious static-field detection; discusses earlier combined AC/DC perception observations.
references.verification: Primary review abstract and human-study table checked. The attachment incorrectly recasts this review as a direct DC+RF experiment establishing VGCC preloading.
references.field: Static electric fields; some included AC/DC perception configurations
references.limits: Review did not establish adverse internal physiological effects of static fields. Its evidence points to a sensory surface route, not 42-fold internal penetration.

references.title: Resonant Convergence: An Integrative Model for Electromagnetic Interactions in Biological Systems
references.finding: Narrative review proposing convergence among ICR-like, QED-coherence, thermomagnetic and related EM mechanisms. It synthesizes hypotheses around shared calcium/calmodulin signalling; it is not an experimental comparison of all mechanisms.
references.verification: Full original XML checked: article-type review-article, published online 31 December 2025, January 2026 collection, volume 27 article 423. Authors explicitly call the work a narrative review.
references.field: Multiple proposed mechanisms; no new joint-exposure protocol
references.limits: Do not count mechanisms converging on one downstream pathway as independent measured gains. Does not map clothing E-field spectra to an ion-cyclotron magnetic-field protocol.

audited_not_selected.title: Stochastic resonance as a possible mechanism of amplification of weak electric signals in living cells
audited_not_selected.assessment: Conceptual discussion/review, not a direct textile+RF or VGCC experiment. Use Bezrukov 1995 for empirical noise-assisted channel transduction.

audited_not_selected.title: Pharmacokinetics of testosterone cream applied to scrotal skin
audited_not_selected.assessment: Original randomized-dose crossover PK study, not merely a TransFemScience review. 12.5/25/50 mg cream; 1.9–2.8 h testosterone peaks, 16 h sampling, endogenous testosterone suppressed with nandrolone. Study compares scrotal doses; it does not directly randomize scrotal versus nonscrotal sites or establish an electromagnetic transmission factor.

audited_not_selected.title: Detection and characterization of microplastics in the human testis and semen
audited_not_selected.assessment: Separate primary study: 6 human testis and 30 semen samples. It is not Hu 2024’s 23 human and 47 canine testes.

chemical_penetration.metric: Relative five-day urinary 14C recovery following topical hydrocortisone
chemical_penetration.unit: ratio; chemical tracer, not EM gain

field_detection.metric: SDT mean detection threshold at 50% humidity
field_detection.note: All 203 participated; threshold-eligible subsets differ. Hybrid number is DC component, not total RMS.

polymer_burden.note: Different donor populations; burden, not measured reproductive impairment in humans.
